title: Pinterest API Pricing: Complete Guide for 2026
snippet:
| Trial access (v5) | Free | Building and testing against a sandbox before launch | Universal cap of 1,000 req/day per app across all endpoints, with `ads_write` stricter at 300/day. Pins are hidden from the public. Product-limited test tokens expire after 24 hours |
| Standard access (v5) | Free | Production publishing, ads, catalogs, analytics | Manual review of a video demo, approval criteria are not published as a fixed checklist |
| Marketing Developer Partners (MDP) | Not publicly priced. Limited, curated program. | Software companies publishing on behalf of brands at scale | Pinterest’s own description calls MDP a “limited, carefully selected group of developer partners” |
| Ads API (inside v5, Standard tier) | Free | Building and reporting on Pinterest ad campaigns at scale | Standard access required, must comply with the developer guidelines’ fee-disclosure rules |

### Trial access (Free)
Pinterest hands every approved developer Trial access after the first review. The point of Trial is to let you call real endpoints with a real OAuth token before you ship.
You get the full endpoint surface (pins, boards, ads, catalogs, analytics, trends) at per-category caps. Test tokens expire after 24 hours, which is the right design for a sandbox and the wrong shape for testing a multi-day workflow.
The catch most teams hit late: Pins created in Trial are hidden from the public. Your code path succeeds, the API returns a Pin ID, the Pin exists in the account, and nobody outside the app can see it. If your QA loop is “post it and check it on the live web,” you’ll think the integration is broken when it isn’t.

### Standard access (Free)
Standard is where production lives. The price is still zero. What changes is the rate-limit shape and the Pin visibility.
To upgrade, you submit a video demo of your app calling the API end-to-end per Pinterest’s [access-tiers upgrade requirements](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/access-tiers/), then wait for a manual review. There is no published timeline. Builders I’ve talked to see the first review come back inside a week when the application is clean and inside three to four weeks when reviewers want changes.

### Marketing Developer Partners (MDP)
The partner track for software companies publishing to Pinterest on behalf of brands at scale. Pinterest launched MDP in 2015 with a small set of partners (Buffer, Tailwind, Sprinklr, and a handful of others) and has kept the program small since.

title: Pinterest Developers | Access tiers
snippet:
The Pinterest API v5 significantly increases the scope of what is possible for you to create as a developer. If approved for API use, your app receives Trial access, which is best for exploring our API features. If you want to offer Pinterest capabilities to your users, we recommend upgrading to Standard access to get the full functionality that our API offers.

access tiers table

|---|---|---|
| Pin Analytics | Yes | Yes |
| Reading ads | Yes | Yes |
| Reading audiences | Yes | Yes |
| Reading boards | Yes | Yes |
| Reading Pins | Yes | Yes |
| Reading catalogs | Yes | Yes |
| Creating ads | Yes | Yes |
| Creating audiences | Yes | Yes |
| Creating boards | Yes (visible only to creator) | Yes |
| Creating Pins | Yes (visible only to creator) | Yes |
| Creating catalogs | Yes | Yes |
| Rate limits | Daily limits based on rate limit category. Please see the section on [Rate Limits](/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/#rate-limits). | Increased rate limits based on activity.

To ensure your app gets approved for Standard access make sure to prep the following:
- Your app must already be approved for Trial access and comply with our [Developer Guidelines](https://policy.pinterest.com/developer-guidelines/).

title: Pinterest API: pins, boards and the approval you need first
snippet:
Two tiers, no others. From Pinterest's [access tiers guide](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/key-concepts/access-tiers/), read today:
| | Trial | Standard |
|---|---|---|
| Positioning | "best for exploring our API features" | "get the full functionality that our API offers" |
| Can read and create | ads, audiences, boards, Pins, catalogs | same |
| Visibility of what you create | boards and Pins visible only to their creator | normal public visibility |
| Rate limit window | daily, per app | per minute, per user, per app |
| All API requests | 1,000 per day | 100 per second per user per app |
| Organic reads (`org_read`) | 1,000 per day | 1,000 per minute |
| Organic writes (`org_write`) | 300 per day | 100 per minute |
| Ads reads (`ads_read`) | 1,000 per day | 1,000 per minute |
| Ads writes (`ads_write`) | 300 per day | 400 per minute |

To move up: the app must already be approved for Trial and comply with the Developer Guidelines, and you submit a video of your app completing an action with the Pinterest API that shows the OAuth flow. That applies even if you are the only user, and terminal or Postman screen recordings are accepted. Pinterest verifies your use case and your privacy policy link during submission. You go to My apps, select **Upgrade** on the app card, confirm the information, upload the video, submit. There is no published timeline: requests are "reviewed regularly" and you get an email with the decision. If it is denied and you appeal through a Help Center ticket, allow "a few days".

Three grants, and only one of them gives you the whole API:
- **Authorization Code**, for acting on a user's behalf. The user approves scopes at `https://www.pinterest.com/oauth/`, lands back on your `redirect_uri` with a code, and your server exchanges it at `oauth/token`. This is the only grant with full API coverage.
- **Client Credentials**, for your own developer account. It requires two-factor authentication and cannot reach some sensitive endpoints.
- **Refresh Token**, to swap a refresh token for a fresh access token with no user involved.
The authorize call wants `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code` and `scope`. `state` is optional and you should send it anyway, since it is what protects the callback from cross-site request forgery.

title: Pinterest Keyword Search Volume API: A Developer Guide
snippet:
- **Do I need partner access?** No partner program is involved. You need a Pinterest developer app with the `ads:read` scope and an ad account the token can see. New apps start on Trial access; production use needs a Standard access review.

## Getting Pinterest API access
Older write-ups, including an earlier version of this one, describe keyword data as "partner access only". In API v5 it is not: the endpoints below are ordinary v5 endpoints, gated on OAuth scopes and your app's access tier.
1. **Create an app** at [developers.pinterest.com](https://developers.pinterest.com/) with a Pinterest business account.
2. **Request scopes.** Keyword metrics, suggested terms and related terms need `ads:read`. The trending keywords endpoint needs `user_accounts:read`.
3. **Have an ad account.** The metrics endpoint lives under `/ad_accounts/{ad_account_id}`, so the authorizing user must have access to one. You do not need to run ads; the metrics are aggregated across all of Pinterest, not your campaigns.
4. **Start on Trial access.** Approved apps begin with Trial access, which has tighter limits and is meant for building and testing.
5. **Apply for Standard access** before you ship to users. The review asks for a screen recording of your app taking a user through the OAuth flow and calling the API.
All endpoints are served from `https://api.pinterest.com/v5` and take a bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

### Do I need Pinterest partner access for keyword data?
No. These are standard v5 endpoints. Apps start on Trial access for building and testing, and need a Standard access review, which includes a recording of your OAuth flow, before shipping to users.
